title: 5. MILK FEVER (Hypocalcemia) & 6. HOOF AND LEG PROBLEMS
text:
5. MILK FEVER (Hypocalcemia)
- Metabolic problem
- Low level of blood calcium
- 24 hours or 2-3 days after calving
- Can lead to other problems like metritis and downer cow syndrome.

Clinical signs:
- Hypersensitivity and excitability.
- Sternal recumbency and anorexic
- Lateral recumbency and loss of consciousness

Treatment:
- Calcium supplementation

6. HOOF AND LEG PROBLEMS – any complication in the hoof and legs may result to lameness.
Common problems:
- Foot rot
- Inter-digital dermatitis

facts: Milk fever is medically termed hypocalcemia.
Milk fever is classified as a metabolic problem.
Milk fever is caused by a low level of blood calcium.
Milk fever typically occurs within 24 hours or 2-3 days after calving.
Milk fever can lead to secondary problems such as metritis and downer cow syndrome.
Clinical signs of milk fever include hypersensitivity and excitability.
Clinical signs of milk fever include sternal recumbency and being anorexic.
Clinical signs of milk fever include lateral recumbency and loss of consciousness.
The primary treatment for milk fever is calcium supplementation.
Any complication in the hoof and legs may result in lameness.
Foot rot is a common hoof and leg problem in dairy cattle.
Inter-digital dermatitis is a common hoof and leg problem in dairy cattle.
